title: India's exports to China jump 39% as core BRICS shipments rise 34% to $19.9 billion
excerpt: Commerce ministry data show shipments to China, South Africa, Brazil and Russia reached $19.9 billion in the first five months of the fiscal year, lifting the bloc's share of India's export basket to 9.2%.
body:
• India's merchandise exports to the four core BRICS economies — China, South Africa, Brazil and Russia — surged 34% to $19.9 billion in April–August 2026-27, up from $14.9 billion a year earlier, commerce ministry data show.
  • China led the expansion, with shipments up 39% to $9.6 billion, driven by engineering goods, electronics and petroleum products; August alone saw a 52% year-on-year jump.
  • South Africa posted the fastest growth at 58% to $4.82 billion, while Brazil rose 13% to $3.46 billion and Russia 11% to $2.04 billion.
  • The four countries' share of India's export basket climbed to 9.2% from 8.1%, underlining a deliberate diversification away from traditional markets.

India's exports to the core founding members of BRICS grew 34 per cent to $19.9 billion in the first five months of 2026-27, led by a 39 per cent surge in shipments to China, the commerce ministry said on Sunday.

The figures cover April–August dispatches to China, South Africa, Brazil and Russia — the bloc's four original non-Indian members — which rose from $14.9 billion in the corresponding period last year. The group's share of India's total merchandise exports climbed to 9.2 per cent from 8.1 per cent.

"As India deepens its engagement with the BRICS bloc, strongest momentum is coming from the BRICS members, especially core BRICS founding partners — China, South Africa, Brazil and Russia," an official said, according to PTI.

China anchors the growth

"The "core BRICS" figures reported by the commerce ministry refer only to the four founding partners besides India."

China was the largest single contributor. Indian exports to China expanded 39 per cent (38.71 per cent on the precise tally) to $9.6 billion, up from $6.93 billion a year earlier. In August alone, shipments to China were up more than 52 per cent year-on-year.

Officials said the surge was driven predominantly by three categories: engineering goods, which contributed 20.73 per cent of the growth; electronic goods at 15.4 per cent; and petroleum products at 13.55 per cent. The expansion comes amid renewed dialogue between New Delhi and Beijing on trade imbalances and supply-chain bottlenecks.

South Africa posted the fastest rate of growth within the group, with shipments jumping 58 per cent to $4.82 billion. Exports to Brazil rose 13 per cent to $3.46 billion, and shipments to Russia increased 11 per cent to $2.04 billion.

Context & Background

BRICS originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, and expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, with Indonesia joining in 2025. The "core BRICS" figures reported by the commerce ministry refer only to the four founding partners besides India.

The bloc's trade push is part of a broader export diversification story. Overall merchandise exports rose 26.12 per cent to $43.81 billion in August, and for the April–August period climbed 17.85 per cent to $215.91 billion. Beyond BRICS, exports to Singapore jumped more than 97 per cent and to Malaysia by over 75 per cent in the five-month period.

Impact & Analysis

The data show India's exporters shifting decisively toward emerging markets. FIEO president S C Ralhan called the broadening of export markets "equally significant" alongside headline growth, saying Indian exporters are "increasingly leveraging new and emerging opportunities while strengthening their presence in traditional markets."

The 39 per cent rise in shipments to China is the standout line, but it comes with an asterisk: India still runs a large structural trade deficit with China, dominated by imports of electronics, machinery and chemicals. The surge is mostly in engineering and manufactured goods, which suggests the imbalance may be narrowing at the margins — though exports of $9.6 billion over five months remain a fraction of what India buys from China.

For trade watchers, the August 52 per cent jump bears watching: it may reflect front-loading of orders, price effects in petroleum products, or genuine demand growth. The commerce ministry's breakdown attributes it largely to manufactured categories, which leans toward the latter.

What's Next

The September trade data, due in mid-October, will show whether the BRICS momentum holds into the festival-season quarter. With merchandise exports running at $215.91 billion for five months, India is on track for another record export year — and the BRICS share of the basket is now firmly above 9 per cent and rising.
